chunks: Ali, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) that
Ali (peace be upon him) allowed the granting of security (aman) by an owned slave to the people of a fort from the forts, and said: 'He is from the believers.'

key_terms.أَمَان: Security/safe-conduct (aman): A guarantee of safety given to enemy combatants, binding upon Muslims once granted
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The believers: The community of faith whose legal standing transcends social status in matters of sacred law
key_terms.حِصْنٌ: Fortress/fort: A fortified defensive position held by the enemy during military engagement
key_terms.عَبْدٌ مَمْلُوكٌ: An owned slave; a person in legal bondage whose civil capacity was restricted under classical Islamic law

ai.seo_question: Can a Muslim slave grant security (aman) to enemy combatants according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) narrates that Imam Ali (AS) upheld the validity of a security pledge (aman) granted by an enslaved Muslim to enemy combatants in a fortress during warfare. This ruling demonstrates that Islamic law recognizes the legal agency of a slave in matters of military security when they act out of their status as a believer. The Imam's justification — 'he is from the believers' — grounds the ruling in the spiritual and legal standing of faith, overriding the slave's social subordination.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that
Ali<sup>asws</sup> allowed the granting of security of an owned slave to the people of a fort from the forts, and said: ‘He is from the Believers’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali has narrated from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once honored the immunity granted by a Muslim slave to the people of a fortress, saying, ‘He is of the believing people.’”
